transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I keep hearing these clear voices. Mostly I hear them in my apartment, but it also happens sometimes when I'm out, like in empty museum rooms. 

It sounds like women whispering from right behind the walls... and they keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's been happening enough that I thought I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been hearing these voices—days, weeks, or months?

It's been a while now. I'd say... about eight months. That's how long I've been hearing the voices, and also how long I've been absolutely certain that people are watching my archive. So, yeah, months. Eight of them.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these voices started?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hit my head, and I don't use drugs or drink. I'm not on any new medications either. It just... started happening on its own.
Since these experiences started, have you noticed any changes in how you're able to manage daily responsibilities, like work, relationships, or taking care of yourself?

Yes, it's... it's definitely affected things. I've missed board meetings, and I haven't been paying my bills. Honestly, I've lost the trust of my colleagues. It got to the point where my cousin and one of the museum administrators had to step in. I just couldn't manage my appointments or handle my money anymore. They didn't think I could handle public events safely on my own, either. So, yes, things have changed a lot.

Besides hearing the voices and feeling watched, have you noticed any changes in how you think or express emotions—like trouble organizing your thoughts, speaking in ways others find hard to follow, or feeling emotionally flat or distant?

Well, my cousin has pointed out that I'm hard to follow lately. If she asks me a simple question, like about a bill or an upcoming doctor's appointment... I try to answer, but I end up talking about the grant money, and then somehow I'm explaining the shipping routes, and then my grandmother's altar. By the time I finish talking, she just looks confused, and nobody seems to know what I actually meant to say. So, yes, I guess I am having trouble keeping my thoughts organized.
Have you noticed any changes in your emotional expression or motivation, such as feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, withdrawing from people, or having a harder time showing emotion?

Yes, I suppose I have. There are long stretches lately where I just sit at my kitchen table... letting the herb pots dry out. I haven't been calling my friends back, either. Even when someone invites me out to things I usually enjoy, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just... I don't feel much interest in going anymore. I just sit there.

Over these past eight months, have you had any distinct periods of feeling extremely low, hopeless, or sad—or on the other end, unusually elated, energetic, or needing much less sleep—that lasted most of the day for a week or more?

Yes, I do have times like that. I get these stretches of days where I feel just... radiant. Like I've been chosen for something important, and I have all this energy for my plans. 

But then, if someone questions what I'm doing or tells me I need to slow down, I become absolutely furious. It's... it feels as if they are trying to erase me. So, yes, I definitely have those periods where I feel incredibly high, and then very angry if anyone gets in my way.

During the times when you are NOT feeling that 'radiant,' high-energy way—that is, when your mood is more normal—do you still hear the whispering voices or still feel that people are watching your archive?

Yes, I do. Actually, there was a stretch of a few weeks not too long ago where I wasn't feeling all that energized or... radiant, like I said before. My mood was pretty normal, I suppose. But even then, I was still hearing the whispering in my apartment. And I was still absolutely certain that the arts people were monitoring my phone calls. So, yes, those things definitely happen even when I'm not having one of those high-energy periods.

Thinking back over the full eight months, would you say the 'radiant,' high-energy periods have taken up most of that time, or have they been relatively brief compared to the times when your mood felt more normal?

I would say they've taken up most of the time. Really, most of these months since I retired have been... well, dominated by those stretches. The times where I feel driven, chosen, and just unable to slow down at all. And irritable, like I mentioned. 

So, yes, even though I've also had some of those quieter, withdrawn days mixed in, those high-energy periods have definitely taken up the majority of the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient has persistent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions for 8 months, meeting Criterion A for schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis. Concurrently, she describes manic episodes (elevated/grandiose mood, decreased need for engagement, increased goal-directed activity, irritability when confronted) that have dominated the majority of the illness duration, satisfying the mood episode requirement for schizoaffective disorder. Critically, she confirmed a distinct period of several weeks with euthymic mood during which the hallucinations and delusions persisted, fulfilling the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of mood episodes for at least 2 weeks. No substance use, medical illness, or other organic cause was identified. This combination—psychosis plus mood episode overlap, with psychosis also occurring independently of mood symptoms, and mood symptoms present for the majority of the illness course—is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than primary Schizophrenia (which would not feature prominent manic episodes for the majority of the illness) or Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychosis persisting during euthymic periods).
